label: rem:np-discrepancy-resolution
title: n/p discrepancy resolution: calibration-dependent, not structural
html:
Remark (neutron-proton discrepancy resolution). The uncalibrated pure-tower formula undershoots the neutron mass due to a \Phi_q pole-distance asymmetry. The free-neutron beta decay prediction must instead use the trace difference directly.

The raw tower prediction relies on per-generator amplitudes that sit at different distances from the q_0 pole. This introduces an artificial scale difference between mirror nucleons. Bypassing the per-nucleon evaluation entirely, the uncalibrated beta-decay Q-value emerges directly from the difference of the Markov normal forms:

  \mathfrak{Q}_\beta = |\Delta(\mathrm{net})| \cdot E_0 \approx 0.7836\;\mathrm{MeV}.

This structural difference evaluates to within 1.3 keV of CODATA. It relies on the topological trace alone, avoiding the single-generator Kashaev approximations.
